figures.caption: Figure 3. Ultrafast pump–probe imaging in WS2/hBN/SiO2 heterostructures. (a) AFM topography of WS2/hBN/SiO2. The domain covered by WS2 is indicated by the white dashed line. (b) A ground-state near-field image at a frequency of 1498 cm-1. (c) Transient near-field images at different delay time 0 ps, 2 ps, and 7 ps at a probe frequency of 1498 cm-1. (d) Profiles of S3 and time-dependent ΔS2 extracted from near-field images of (b) and (c).

Figure 2. Demonstration of polariton imaging using broadband light pulse. (a) Experimental setup for ultrafast nano-imaging of polaritons. BS: ZnSe beam splitter, OAP: off-axis parabolic mirror, ωAFM: tapping frequency of the AFM tip, Ωchop: chopper frequency, Δtref: reference delay. (b) AFM topography and SNOM image demodulated at 3ωAFM (S3) of hBN/SiO2 at the frequency of 1477 cm-1 and 1517 cm-1. (c) Dispersion relationship of phonon polaritons in hBN (147 nm)/SiO2. White circles indicate experimental data obtained by fringe period in (b).
Figure 1. Ultrafast control of hyperbolic phonon polaritons. Hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hBN are modulated by visible-pump-induced generation of electron–hole pairs in WS2.

Figure 5. Numerical simulations by FEM. (a) Calculation geometry of WS2/hBN/SiO2 (left) and hBN/WS2/SiO2 (right). The dipole source is located at 300 nm above the hBN surface. Figure 4. Ultrafast pump–probe imaging in hBN/WS2/SiO2 heterostructures. (a) AFM topography of the hBN/WS2/SiO2 sample. The thicknesses of the hBN and WS2 layers are 38 nm and 376 nm, respectively. The inset shows the structure of the sample. (b–c) Ground- (b) and transient-state (c) near-field images at a frequency of 1425 cm⁻¹. The white dashed line indicates the location where the profile shown in (d) was extracted. (d) Fringe profiles of S3 and ΔS2 obtained from (b) and (c). The polaritonic wavelengths (λₚ) were evaluated to be 570 nm and 660 nm for S₃ and ΔS₂, respectively, based on the fittings (green line). (e) λp of S3 and ΔS2 extracted from the fringe profiles as a function of detection frequency (ω).
